text:
Alessa H: quick q — when creating an experiment in Console via the wizard, what should the default variant seeding strategy be? should we do equal weights or bias toward control?
Mike T: leaning toward bias to control for multi-variant tests to avoid diluting signals. default 70/30 control/first-variant? :thinking_face:
Sanjay K: 70/30 seems fine for 2 variants. but for >2 variants that feels ad-hoc. maybe a strategy: control gets 50% and remaining split evenly?
Jana R: major concern is very small segments — if user routes 1% of traffic to experiment, 50/25/25 is pointless. we should normalize by absolute traffic. if expected users < X, force binary canary only.
Alessa H: good point. proposal: seed strategy = {"control_first": true, "min_effective_users": 200, "control_weight": 0.6} and UI shows explanation + tooltip.
Liam P: +1. Also need server-side guards: per-variant qps cap and hard fallback to control when latency SLO degrades. otherwise customers shoot themselves in foot.
Mike T: agreed. small sketch of guard config we could store on experiment model:
```yaml
guard_policy:
  min_requests: 500
  slo_degradation_pct: 8  # if error/latency increases >8% vs baseline
  per_variant_qps_cap: 50
  fallback: control
```
Jana R: can we make min_requests adaptive? e.g. min_requests = max(global_min, expected_daily_users * 0.01) — that keeps things useful for high-traffic flows.
Sanjay K: yeah compute expected_daily_users from route telemetry. default global_min 200. also we should suggest using "staged ramp" template: 1% -> 10% -> target over configurable windows.
Alessa H: UI ideas: when user adds variants, show a compact preview: "seed: control 60%, others split equally (or custom)" and a recommended ramp button that creates three sequential phases.
Mike T: API param name suggestion: `seed_strategy` with enum values ["equal","control_biased","traffic_proportional"], plus `ramp_template_id`. backend applies guards and writes telemetry hooks.
Liam P: telemetry hooks are critical: we need per-variant counters, p50/p95 latency, error rate, and a derived "regression_score" to trigger automated rollback. also annotate events with rollout_stage and allocation so dashboards can correlate.
DeployBot: experiment:create event 1718362410 recorded (meta: user=alessa.h, source=console-wizard)
Jana R: UX microcopy: under seed weights add: "We recommend biasing toward control for initial seeds to preserve statistical power. Use ramp templates to safely reach target allocations." small link to docs.
Sanjay K: one more API nit: when user passes exact variant weights via API, we should still attach guard_policy unless they explicitly disable it. opt-out must be explicit and require org-admin perms.
Alessa H: action items: Mike add API enum + backend defaults; Jana draft microcopy + tooltip; Liam add telemetry event spec; Sanjay implement adaptive min_requests; I'll wire UI preview and ramp button.
Mike T: putting PRs on my board for API + backend defaults. will ping when ready. :thumbsup:
Liam P: I'll sketch the prometheus labels and event schema later today.
Jana R: I'll mock up tooltip copy in Figma and drop screenshots here.
Alessa H: thanks team — sounds like a good default plan. we can always iterate after a small beta. :rocket:
